notes.title: Purple Noise Echo - Release Date
notes.notes:
It's been a while since I posted any news here. I have been developing Purple Noise Echo in my spare time for several years now. 
Progress has been slow, but step by step I have reached this special moment:

I'm pleased to announce that the game is now in its final stage and will be officially released on May 25th!

[previewyoutube=5eot0HPpocQ;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: update 0.43
notes.notes:
Hello,

This is probably the biggest update I've done so far. 
I've been working on a lot of bugs, but I've also improved and completed all the systems of the game. 
There are new effects, feedback improvements, animations, sound effects, new meshes... but most of all the game is playable from start to finish, only the final level is not fully implemented.
We can say that the game is really in beta stage. 
This is a really important step for this side project that I've been working on alone for a while now.
The next steps, which separate the game from a full release, are the implementation of the save system, a qualitative improvement of the whole game and of course a ruthless bug hunt!

I hope that the game experience will be up to the expectations, and even more than usual the comments and feedbacks of beta-testers are important in this final stretch!

notes.title: update 0.42
notes.notes:
Hi,

Quick patch this week.

- Fixed the GameOver screen where interactions can sometimes get stuck.
- Some minor corrections.

Thanks

notes.title: update 0.41
notes.notes:
Hi,

0.41 is a general update of the game, with lots of bug fixes and improvements on all game systems. 
And a special focus on the UI of the HUD and the menu.

As always, don't hesitate to send me your feedback and comments!

Thanks.

notes.title: Update 0.40
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

It's been a long time since there has been an update, too long... The last few months, my work as a solo and freelance developer has taken up all my time and energy.

The new update is finally here. 

In this one, I've been chasing the inevitable bugs that are hiding in every corner. And I focused my attention on the game's handling and understanding. Purple Noise Echo is and will remain a game that requires you to understand by yourself its universe and its mechanics. But I tried to simplify it wherever possible, in order to find the right balance. So there are essentially changes in the interface, and in the units behavior.

In addition, because an indie game should remain accessible, I optimized the code as much as possible and I changed the rendering of the game, so that it runs well, even on a small configuration... hopefully.

It's a work in progress, but I'm starting to see the finish line on the horizon! 

Thank you for the work!

notes.title: Update 0.39
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

This update adds some UI improvement and some effects. But most importantly, I've changed the way the game is rendered. So the lights and post-effects are much better. There is a cost, which I hope is not too high. I have to fine-tune it to be fully satisfied with the colours and lighting, the atmosphere of the environment is something important in the game. 
If you have an opinion on this graphic change, let me know! 

Now that all the features are in the game, I will spend all my available time to bring it to a decent quality level! Fixing bugs of course, improving the effects, adding sound effects and background music, adding some animations and integrating the narration! 
It's still a huge amount of work!

As you may know, I'm working alone on this game, and I work full time as a freelance game developer and I have to take care of my family. So sometimes it's hard to find the time and energy to work on the game the way I want, and my estimate for a full release seems to be constantly being pushed back, and doubt is everywhere! 

So if you have any comments, feel free to send them to me! 
The whole point of independent gaming is to share an experience with players, so if you think this game is interesting, please spread the word! :)

Thanks!

notes.title: Update 0.38
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

Today, I'm happy to announce that all levels of Purple Noise Echo are now into the game! This means that all the mechanics have been integrated!

I still have one main feature left to put in the game, but on that point I won't say more for now... :)

I will now focus on the sound design, the visuals and of course the debugging. 

Thanks to all of you for your support and comments that allow me to improve my game and hold on as a solo developer.

See you soon for more news!

notes.title: Update 0.37
notes.notes:
This update took a lot of time, more than I expected. But it's here!

I added several levels with new challenges, new units and skills. Saying more about them will spoil the game. They're here to be discovered!  
Besides, I fixed bugs, cleaned up some code and tried to improve some systems.
I'm still focusing on level design, code and systems for now... It's almost done, just a couple more updates! 
Then I'll focus on the visuals and sounds! 

As usual, any feedback is more than welcome. As you may know, I'm working alone on this project next to my freelance work, so the more feedback I get, the more problems I fix! 

Have a good game!

notes.title: Update 0.35
notes.notes:
​This update introduces the game map system.

It takes more refactoring of the code than I thought, but now datas are handle in a more efficient way and it lead the path to the save game system.

Now that its done I expect to deliver updates on a more regular basis!

notes.title: Update 0.34
notes.notes:
This update focuses on optimization and ergonomics.

The most notable change is the way energy is consumed when performing a displacement action. Until now, each movement has consumed a little energy. From now on, by default, units will no longer consume energy when moving, unless they are injured. The more damaged they are, the more energy they lose. 

In addition to that and bug fixes, I tried to improve the readability and balance of the colors. It is still a work in progress....

- Change in the logic of energy consumption on unit movements.
- When Node moves before the companions reach their target destination, their new path is now calculated correctly.
- When a companion a level, the accessibility of the tiles is correctly recalculated.
- When a companion is selected and a plugin is added to the grid is now reset.
- In sticky mode, if a companion does not have a direct path to Node, he looks for the tile as close as possible to Node.

notes.title: Update 0.33
notes.notes:
This is the first update after EA launch on Steam, the Indie Game Factory & IndieCade Europe events.

It focuses on optimization, bug fixes (mainly related to unit behavior) and UX.

One of the things that has come out of the feedback over the last few days is the difficulty some players have in understanding some of the game's mechanisms. It's a game where you have to discover the potential of the gameplay as you go by, but I'm working to make it as understandable as possible is this and the next updates.

[Optimization] - Rewriting a part of the grid and the behavior code
[Bug fix] - Units leaving the levels did not update the position of the tiles.
[Bug fix] - The path between keys and doors was no longer highlighted.
[Bug fix] - The units' behavior was blocked when they had no possible movement.
[Bug fix] - Tracking a companion's behavior has an incorrect calculation path
[Bug fix] - The follow behavior in sticky mode tends to go on the same tile as Node.
[Gameplay] - The follow behavior of the companion is now set to "sticky" by default.
[Gameplay] - The energy is recharged to a minimum of 50% when entering a new level.
[UI] - New cursor implementation
[UI] - The tile highlights have a new design and behavior
[UI] - The "Re-Sync" alert is no longer useful and has been deleted.
[Design] - The doors now have a more closed design
[Design] - Redesign of "tutorial" levels to be more concentrated and compartmentalized
